theater: 西西里島與墨西拿海峽

battle.name: 第一次布匿戰爭
battle.theater: 西西里島與墨西拿海峽
battle.brief: 公元前264年，麥西那的馬梅爾提尼傭兵向羅馬求救，羅馬在無海軍的情況下一年內仿造希臘五列槳船造出艦隊，用登船橋把海戰變成甲板上的方陣對決，與迦太基在西西里島苦戰二十三年。希臘式重步兵方陣是兩軍步兵的共同底盤：迦太基靠希臘傭兵與斯巴達人贊提普改造的馬其頓方陣，羅馬則以脫胎自方陣的軍團應戰。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前264年至前241年羅馬共和國與迦太基城邦聯盟之間、以西西里島為主戰場的長期對抗，前後二十三年，是西方地中海最早的一場大規模跨海戰爭。羅馬一方由元老院與百人團大會授權，兩名執政官輪流統兵，採執政官雙軍制：每人各領兩個公民軍團，軍團以百人隊為基本單位，分為少年兵、主力兵與老兵三列，兩翼由拉丁盟邦與伊特魯里亞的輔兵填補，騎兵由公民騎士與盟邦騎士合編；全軍總數在開戰之初約七萬六千步兵與六千騎兵，其後因戰損與補員而膨脹，制度上的弱點是指揮分散、部隊年年輪換，難以連續經營同一戰區。迦太基一方的權力核心是由 suffete 與百餘名議員組成的會議，主戰期間多由家族將領統兵，如漢尼拔·吉斯可、哈米爾·巴卡與哈諾；兵源以腓尼基市民兵、伊比利亞的西班牙傭兵、努米底亞輕騎與利比福尼基非洲步兵為主，並大量僱用希臘與馬其頓式重步兵。西西里島的各城邦並非旁觀者，阿克拉加斯、帕諾爾穆斯、塞利農圖先後結盟或倒戈，敘拉古的國王希埃隆二世自始站在羅馬一方，而麥西那的馬梅爾提尼傭兵團求援，正是把羅馬拖進戰爭的引信。
countriesEn: This war was a long contest between the Roman Republic and the coalition of the city-state of Carthage, fought over Sicily and the Strait of Messina between 264 and 241 BC; it ran for twenty-three years and was the first large-scale overseas war in the western Mediterranean. On the Roman side power was vested in the senate and the comitia centuriata, and two consuls commanded in rotation under the consular army system: each consul led two citizen legions, the legions were built up from maniples of sixty men, divided into the hastati, the principes and the triarii, and their flanks were filled in by contingents of the Latin League and the Etruscans, while the cavalry was drawn jointly from Roman knights and the horsemen of the allies; the total force stood at about seventy-six thousand foot and six thousand horse at the opening of the war and swelled afterwards through losses and replacements, the institutional weakness being dispersed command and the yearly rotation of troops, which made it hard to run one theatre of operations continuously. At Carthage the centre of power was the council of the suffetes and more than a hundred members, and during the war the command was usually held by commanders of leading houses, such as Hannibal Gisco, Hamilcar Barca and Hanno; the troops came from Punic citizen levies, Iberian mercenary levies from Spain, Numidian light horse and Libyphoenician infantry from Africa, with large numbers of Greek and Macedonian-style heavy infantry taken on contract. The cities of Sicily were not bystanders either: Akragas, Panormos and Segesta entered alliances or changed sides in turn, the king of Syracuse, Hieron II, stood with Rome from the beginning, and the appeal of the Mamertine mercenaries of Messana was the fuse that dragged Rome into the war.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩邊。羅馬方面，前264年的執政官阿皮烏斯·克勞狄烏斯·凱庫斯是真正的推手：他判定海戰無法迴避，主張由國庫出錢造船；據波利比烏斯記載，他派往希臘的使團在克尼杜斯受熱情招待，希臘人故意在宴後搬走支撐大廳的柱子，讓使團無法近前觀看三列槳的樣船，羅馬人回國後仍照樣仿出五列槳船。前260年的執政官蓋烏斯·杜伊利烏斯在米拉海戰中以右翼迂迴取勝，凱旋柱上刻有雄雞圖樣，後世遂以雄雞為海軍的吉祥記號；前256年的兩名執政官蓋烏斯·阿提利烏斯·雷古盧斯與盧基烏斯·曼利烏斯·武爾索在埃克諾穆斯海戰以展開的長列艦隊取得慘勝；前250年的執政官盧基烏斯·科爾涅利烏斯·西庇奧·阿西納在埃加迪亞群島取勝，卻在米利海峽追擊時中伏而失明；前241年的執政官盧基烏斯·盧塔蒂烏斯·卡圖盧斯在埃加特斯群島擊敗哈諾，取得羅馬史上第一次海軍凱旋。迦太基方面，前255年自希臘請來的斯巴達人贊提普重整軍隊，操練成馬其頓式密集方陣，在帕諾爾穆斯擊潰執政官卡拉提努斯，旋遭本國當權者處死；前247年哈米爾·巴卡奪取埃里克斯山，切斷西西里西部的道路；前241年哈諾在最後一役大敗而被本國放逐。此外還有大量未留下姓名的職業軍人：登船橋後待命的羅馬軍團士兵、駕著撞角船反覆衝撞的迦太基水手，以及在埃里克斯山下因欠餉而拒絕解除武裝的西班牙傭兵。
peopleEn: The decisive figures fall on both sides. On the Roman side, the consul of 264 BC, Appius Claudius Caecus, was the real driving force: he judged that a naval war could not be avoided and argued for building a fleet at public expense; according to Polybius, the embassy he sent to Greece was warmly received at Cnidus, where the Greeks deliberately removed a column that supported the hall after the banquet so that the envoys could not get near enough to study the three-banked model ship, and the Romans went home and built a five-banked quinquereme all the same. The consul of 260 BC, Gaius Duilius, won the battle of Mylae by turning his right wing inwards, and the rooster carved on his triumphal column made the bird the lucky sign of the Roman navy ever after; the two consuls of 256 BC, Gaius Atilius Regulus and Lucius Manlius Vulso, won the desperately fought naval battle of Ecnomus with a line deployed at length; the consul of 250 BC, Lucius Cornelius Scipio Asina, won in the Aegadian Islands and then was ambushed and blinded while pursuing the enemy in the straits of Mylae; the consul of 241 BC, Lucius Lutatius Catulus, defeated Hanno at the Aegates Islands and won the first naval triumph in Roman history. On the Carthaginian side, the Spartan Xanthippus, brought over from Greece in 255 BC, reorganised the army and drilled it into the dense Macedonian phalanx, destroyed the consular army of Calatinus at Panormus, and was then put to death by the Carthaginian authorities; in 247 BC Hamilcar Barca seized Mount Eryx and cut the roads in western Sicily; in 241 BC Hanno was beaten in the last battle and exiled by his own state. Alongside them stand the many professionals who left no name: the legionaries waiting behind the boarding bridges, the Carthaginian sailors driving the ram again and again, and the Spanish mercenaries under the walls of Eryx who refused to lay down their arms because their pay was in arrears.
kits: 卡面這件希臘重步兵的裝備是青銅時代晚期的典型組合：頭戴科林斯式青銅盔，身披亞麻襯底加青銅片的線襯胸甲或肌肉式胸甲，小腿與大腿加護脛與護腿，手持直徑約九十公分的圓盾 aspis（hoplon），腰佩短劍 xiphos，右手持二至二點七公尺長的長矛 dory，矛頭為鐵、帶青銅套箍。公元前500年的這套裝備到公元前264年已過時數百年，但它所代表的作戰體系仍在西西里決定勝負：重步兵方陣以盾緣交疊、互相遮蔽為核心，縱深排列使投射兵器難以打散正面，迦太基的希臘傭兵以此為骨幹，贊提普更把手軍整成馬其頓式方陣。羅馬的軍團則是方陣的變體：少年兵以長標槍 pilum 集體投射，掩護主力兵接近至盾與劍的距離，後方老兵接應，其靈活性來自縱深階梯式的分隊，而不是希臘式的整面重合。真正的分野在海：迦太基戰艦裝青銅撞角與多列划槳，側舷加掛抓鉤，擅長撞擊後接舷肉搏；羅馬本無海軍，便仿造五列槳船 quinquereme，每船編制約三百人、其中約一百二十名為軍團士兵，船上裝寬約一點二公尺、頂端有鐵蒺藜的登船橋 corvus，正是靠它把水戰變成甲板上的方陣對決。攻城方面，羅馬人自阿克拉加斯圍城起造出配備撞木、箭塔與投石機的攻城器械，迦太基人則以築壘挖溝與土牆對抗，雙方都精於環形塹壕與胸牆。
kitsEn: The Greek hoplite on the card wears the standard kit of the late Bronze Age: a Corinthian bronze helmet, a linen corselet faced with bronze plates or a muscle cuirass, greaves and thigh guards, a round shield of about ninety centimetres across, the aspis or hoplon, a short sword, the xiphos, at the hip, and in the right hand a thrusting spear two to two and a half metres long, the dory, with an iron head and a bronze ferrule. By 264 BC that equipment was several centuries out of date, but the system of war it stood for still decided things in Sicily: the hoplite phalanx rested on overlapping shields that shielded one another, and its depth made it hard to break with missiles, the Greek mercenaries of Carthage formed its backbone, and Xanthippus turned the whole army into a Macedonian-style phalanx. The Roman legion was a variant of the phalanx: the hastati threw their long pila in massed volleys, covering the principes as they closed to sword and shield range, with the triarii supporting from behind, and its flexibility came from the stepped depth of separate maniples rather than from a single solid front. The real dividing line lay at sea: Carthaginian ships carried bronze rams and banks of oars with grappling hooks along the flanks, and they were built to ram and then board; Rome had no navy at all, so she copied the quinquereme, each hull of about three hundred men of whom some hundred and twenty were legionaries, and fitted her ships with the corvus, a boarding bridge about a metre and a quarter wide with an iron spike at the far end, and it was the corvus that turned a naval battle into a phalanx fight on a deck. On the siege side, the Romans built a train of battering rams, arrow towers and stone-throwers for the siege of Akragas, while the Carthaginians answered with embankments, ditches and earthen ramparts; both sides were skilled in the circumvallation and the covered way.
tactics: 羅馬開戰時沒有制海權，戰術的起點是把海陸問題倒過來解決：先想辦法在海峽登陸與補給，再解決怎樣在陸上頂住迦太基的援軍。艦隊建成後，羅馬採縱列橫陳：戰線分作三段，右翼先以一艘旗艦接戰，中隊與左翼依次展開，拉成數十艘的長線，以免被迦太基集中撞擊；米拉海戰中杜伊利烏斯在接戰前把右翼折向岸邊，變成迂迴的螺旋陣形，避開迦太基撞角的正面衝撞。登船橋讓羅馬的投射兵與劍士在接舷瞬間湧上敵舷，戰役遂由撞角競賽變成甲板上的方陣對決。埃克諾穆斯海戰中，羅馬以兩支艦隊分置兩翼、每翼六十餘艘，分階段切入迦太基密集的縱隊，逼出一場延續數日的立體戰。陸上，執政官各領一軍，四千八百人的公民軍團置中，拉丁盟邦與伊特魯里亞步兵分列兩翼，騎兵在最外側；交戰以標槍在三十至六十公尺齊射，然後壓進至盾距，靠短劍與盾緣互推消耗。迦太基在帕諾爾穆斯的反制很清楚：贊提普拒絕讓中央方陣單獨受衝，堅持讓兩翼的非洲步兵與努米底亞騎兵先拖住羅馬騎兵，待其分離後方陣才以整面重合的盾線推進，羅馬軍心一散，陣形裂開，整軍被切斷。羅馬此後長期以環形塹壕與圍城線作戰，並最終把重心由陸戰轉向封鎖海上交通，用圍城消耗埃里克斯山守軍。
tacticsEn: Rome began the war without command of the sea, so the problem of strategy had to be turned inside out: first find a way to cross the strait and keep the army supplied, and only then work out how to hold the ground against Carthaginian reinforcements. Once the fleet existed, the Romans formed line ahead: the battle line was divided into three sections, the right wing engaging first with a flagship, the centre and left deployed in turn and stretched into a line of several tens of ships, so that the Carthaginians could not concentrate their rams on one point; at Mylae, Duilius bent his right wing back towards the land before contact, forming an oblique or spiral formation that dodged the frontal charge of the Carthaginian rams. The corvus let Roman missile troops and swordsmen swarm over the enemy deck at the moment of contact, so that the battle became a phalanx fight on a deck rather than a contest of rams. At Ecnomus the Romans split into two wings of sixty-odd ships each and cut into the dense Carthaginian lines in stages, producing a multi-day fight in three dimensions. On land, each consul led one army, with a citizen legion of four thousand eight hundred men in the centre, the infantry of the Latin League and the Etruscans on the flanks, and the cavalry outside them; the fighting opened with a volley of pila at thirty to sixty metres, after which the line pressed to shield range and ground itself down with sword and shield. The Carthaginian answer at Panormus was clear: Xanthippus refused to let the central phalanx be charged alone, insisting that the African infantry and the Numidian horse on the wings engage the Roman cavalry first and only advancing the solid front of overlapping shields once the Roman flanks had been drawn apart; the Roman line lost its cohesion, the formation split, and the whole army was cut off. Rome then fought for years behind a circumvallation and a line of siege works, and finally shifted the weight of the war from the land to the sea, cutting the communications of the garrison on Eryx by blockade and siege.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下。戰爭自公元前264年打到前241年，共二十三年，是羅馬有史以來最長的一場戰爭。波利比烏斯在開戰之初估計的兵力是：羅馬步兵約七萬六千、騎兵約六千，迦太基步兵約七萬、騎兵約一萬二千；他並記下此時羅馬把服役年限延至十六年。羅馬第一支艦隊據波利比烏斯與老普林尼記載為一百艘五列槳船加二百艘較小的船，開赴米拉的第一批只有十七艘，載兵一萬。前256年埃克諾穆斯海戰是古代地中海規模最大的交戰，雙方合計約一千三百艘船；波利比烏斯記迦太基損失約七百艘，羅馬全役另計約七百艘，舊船靠繳獲重建，可見羅馬真正的瓶頸是錢而非木料。前263年羅馬開始向公民財產徵收特別稅以維持戰費，軍營制度與工程兵的專業化也始於此役。圍城方面，阿克拉加斯之圍前後約半載，帕諾爾穆斯在前255年與前250年兩度易手，前250年開啟的利利巴埃姆圍城則延續到前241年，長達十年。終局是前241年的埃加特斯群島海戰，羅馬以約三百艘五列槳船迎擊迦太基分隊，迦太基全軍覆沒；和約條件是放棄西西里宗主權，並在十年內支付二百萬德拉克馬賠款，據波利比烏斯，當時迦太基在伊比利亞銀礦的年產約五萬德拉克馬，另有其他礦山一年約十萬，賠款大約等於兩年的礦產總量。前240年卡圖盧斯的凱旋是羅馬史上第一次海軍凱旋。戰中數名執政官陣亡或被俘，蓋烏斯·阿提利烏斯·雷古盧斯於前255年被俘，數年後死於迦太基的囚禁之中。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The war ran from 264 BC to 241 BC, twenty-three years in all, the longest war the Romans had yet fought. The strength Polybius gives at the opening of the war is about seventy-six thousand foot and six thousand horse for Rome, and about seventy thousand foot and twelve thousand horse for Carthage; he also notes that the Romans at this time extended the term of military service to sixteen years. Rome's first fleet, according to Polybius and Pliny the Elder, was a hundred quinqueremes together with two hundred smaller vessels, and the first contingent to sail for Mylae was a squadron of seventeen ships carrying ten thousand men. The naval battle of Ecnomus in 256 BC was the largest engagement in the ancient Mediterranean, with about thirteen hundred ships on both sides; Polybius records a loss of some seven hundred ships on the Carthaginian side, while Rome lost about seven hundred over the whole war, its old hulls being rebuilt from what was captured, so that the true bottleneck for Rome was money rather than timber. In 263 BC the Romans began levying a special tax on the property of citizens to pay for the war, and the system of the marching camp and the professionalisation of engineer troops also date from this campaign. On the siege side, the siege of Akragas lasted roughly half a year, Panormus changed hands in 255 BC and again in 250 BC, and the siege of Lilybaeum, opened in 250 BC, ran on to 241 BC, a full ten years. The end came at the Aegates Islands in 241 BC, where some three hundred Roman quinqueremes met a Carthaginian detachment and the Carthaginian fleet was destroyed. The terms were the renunciation of all claim to Sicily and the payment of two million drachmas in ten annual instalments; according to Polybius, the Carthaginian silver mines of Iberia were then producing about fifty thousand drachmas a year and the other mines about a hundred thousand, so that the indemnity amounted to roughly two years of total mineral output. Catulus' triumph in 240 BC was the first naval triumph in Roman history. Several consuls were killed or captured during the war, and Gaius Atilius Regulus, taken prisoner in 255 BC, died some years later in Carthaginian captivity.
cause: 直接導火線是麥西那的一次請援。迦太基將軍哈諾以本國軍隊協助敘拉古的暴君阿加托克勒斯奪取西西里東岸的港口城鎮讚克勒，該地後來被一幫坎帕尼亞傭兵佔領，這批傭兵就是馬梅爾提尼。他們屠殺城內居民後與敘拉古決裂，被哈諾的迦太基軍隊圍困，向迦太基求援不成，最後派使者越過海峽向羅馬求救。羅馬立刻接手有三個具體原因。其一是地緣：麥西那扼住墨西拿海峽，是西西里與義大利之間最便捷的渡口，誰控制海峽誰就控制島上的貿易與糧食。其二是羅馬在南義大利的希臘城邦已有駐軍與盟約，麥西那原是羅馬一方的盟友城市，羅馬不能坐視盟友被拆吞。其三是迦太基的海上力量若控制西西里東岸，義大利南部的穀物與陶業商路就會暴露在敵人面前，敘拉古的希埃隆二世也立刻派騎兵隊馳援羅馬。深一層看，這是迦太基商業帝國與羅馬地中海霸權的第一次攤牌：迦太基不願放棄西西里，羅馬不肯容忍迦太基的勢力越過海峽，而雙方都明白一旦開戰就不會速決，因為迦太基以海軍與傭兵立國，羅馬以步兵與公民團結立國，誰都沒有對方的長處。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was an appeal for help from Messana. The Carthaginian general Hanno had used the army of Carthage to help the tyrant of Syracuse, Agathocles, take the port town of Zancle on the eastern coast of Sicily, and the place was later occupied by a band of Campanian mercenaries, the Mamertines. After killing the townsmen they fell out with Syracuse, were besieged by Hanno's Carthaginian force, failed to obtain help from Carthage, and finally sent envoys across the strait to ask Rome for assistance. Rome took the matter up at once for three concrete reasons. The first was geography: Messana commands the Strait of Messina, the most convenient crossing between Sicily and Italy, and whoever holds the strait holds the trade and the grain of the island. The second was that Rome already had garrisons and treaties among the Greek cities of southern Italy, Messana had been a city friendly to Rome, and Rome could not sit still while an ally was carved up. The third was that if the Carthaginian sea power held the eastern coast of Sicily, the grain and pottery routes of southern Italy would lie exposed to the enemy, and the king of Syracuse, Hieron II, sent a squadron of cavalry to support Rome at once. At a deeper level this was the first confrontation between the commercial empire of Carthage and the Mediterranean ascendancy of Rome: Carthage would not give up Sicily, Rome would not tolerate Carthaginian power across the strait, and both understood that once the war began it would not be quick, since Carthage was a seafaring state of mercenaries and Rome a state of infantry and citizen levies, and neither had the other's strength.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果超出西西里本身。對迦太基而言，二十三年的消耗加上最後的賠款，等於把海上商路的優勢拱手讓人，其在西西里以東的霸權結束，義大利西岸的貿易線轉入羅馬控制；更嚴重的是前241年之後尚未解散的僱傭兵隊在埃里克斯山下要求遣散費並拒絕解除武裝，哈斯德魯巴爾（人稱法官）以努米底亞騎兵鎮壓，開啟了前241至前238年那場被稱為無名戰爭的非洲內戰，迦太基的邊境在非洲陷於混亂，此後再無力與羅馬在西方地中海長期競爭。對羅馬而言，西西里成為第一個行省，羅馬第一次擁有一支常備海軍與一整套海軍戰術：登船橋的用法、縱列橫陳的線形，以及登船即登陸的思路，後來在第二次布匿戰爭對付迦太基戰艦時被原樣搬出來。軍事理論上，本役留下方陣對軍團的長久辯論：前250年帕諾爾穆斯的敗績，使羅馬人相信方陣不可輕敵，也讓軍團中隊制以靈活性取勝的傳統被重新肯定，這一辯論要到前197年庫諾斯刻法勒與前168年皮德納的會戰才有結論。制度上，二十三年的海外用兵逼出羅馬的財政稅制、工程兵種與軍營制度的成熟，也第一次把公民兵拉出義大利的城界，長期遠征成為常態。從更長的歷史看，羅馬與迦太基的第一次全面碰撞證明了地中海的霸權只能屬於一方。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reached well beyond Sicily. For Carthage, twenty-three years of expenditure and the indemnity at the end amounted to handing over the advantage of the sea routes, and its hegemony east of Sicily came to an end, with the trade of the western Italian coast passing under Roman control; more seriously, the mercenary army that was still under arms after 241 BC demanded its discharge pay at the foot of Eryx and refused to lay down its weapons, and Hasdrubal, called the Judge, put them down with the aid of the Numidian horse, opening the African civil war of 241 to 238 BC that is called the Truceless War, so that the Carthaginian frontier in Africa fell into confusion and Carthage never again had the strength to contest the western Mediterranean with Rome for long. For Rome, Sicily became the first province, and Rome possessed for the first time a standing navy and a complete doctrine of naval warfare: the use of the corvus, the line deployed at length, and the idea that boarding is landing were all carried over unchanged when Roman ships met Carthaginian ones in the Second Punic War. In military theory the war left a long-running debate between phalanx and legion: the defeat at Panormus in 250 BC convinced the Romans that a phalanx must not be underestimated, and confirmed the Roman tradition that the maniple won through flexibility, a debate that was settled only at Cynoscephalae in 197 BC and Pydna in 168 BC. Institutionally, twenty-three years of overseas war forced the maturity of Roman taxation, of engineer troops and of the marching camp, and for the first time took the citizen levy out of the towns of Italy, making long campaigning normal. Over the longer run, the first full collision of Rome and Carthage proved that the dominion of the Mediterranean could belong to only one of them.
result: 公元前241年的和約結束了戰爭，結果對迦太基近乎苛刻：放棄西西里島與周邊島嶼的宗主權，十年內分期支付二百萬德拉克馬賠款，撤去海上部署，承認羅馬在西西里的一切處置；迦太基保住北非本土、西班牙的據點、撒丁島與巴利阿里群島，卻失去了西地中海的生意與它先前在西西里徵收的稅源。羅馬這邊保留西西里全境與主要城邦，希埃隆二世統治下的敘拉古成為羅馬在島上的附庸，島嶼被劃為第一個行省，由帶杖的總督管治；羅馬艦隊在凱旋後縮編但仍留在軍械庫，成為西地中海第一支常備海軍，而它帶來的戰爭債務與稅負，讓羅馬在往後兩百年間屢次面臨遠征愈遠、駐軍愈多的循環。前241至前238年的非洲僱傭兵戰爭幾乎耗盡迦太基殘存的國力，戰後的迦太基重建了對西班牙銀礦的依賴，這條依賴日後在第二次布匿戰爭中又把兩個國家拖到一起。若只論這一場戰役本身的勝負，羅馬以海軍的後發優勢、公民步兵的韌性與長期的圍城戰術贏得了西西里，迦太基則輸在把海峽與島嶼的爭奪變成一場比它更能承受消耗的戰爭。
resultEn: The peace of 241 BC ended the war, and the terms were harsh for Carthage: the renunciation of all sovereignty over Sicily and the islands around it, the payment of two million drachmas in ten annual instalments, the withdrawal of the fleet, and unconditional recognition of whatever Rome decided in Sicily. Carthage kept North Africa itself, its Spanish possessions, Sardinia and the Balearic islands, but lost the western Mediterranean trade and the tribute it had been drawing from Sicily. Rome kept the whole island and its principal cities, Syracuse under Hieron II became a client of Rome on the island, Sicily was constituted the first province of the republic, administered by a governor of consular rank, and the Roman fleet, though reduced after the triumph, was kept in the dockyards and became the first standing navy of the western Mediterranean; the war debts and the new taxes it required would put Rome into a recurring condition, over the following two centuries, of campaigns reaching further and garrisons growing. The African mercenary war of 241 to 238 BC very nearly used up what strength Carthage had left, and the state rebuilt itself on the silver of Spain, a dependence that was to drag the two states together again in the Second Punic War. If the result of this war alone is judged, Rome won Sicily on the strength of a navy built at the last moment, the resilience of its citizen infantry and the patience of long sieges, while Carthage lost because it had turned a dispute over a strait and an island into a war of attrition that it could not afford.
